notes:
[TXT028-construction] Manuscript page 27 opens with a locally cancelled Proposition and a live setup sentence. The abandoned construction below uses nonempty intersections A°∩B° and calls the induced equivalence relation a “borne sup”. That cancelled argument is transcribed, not certified. The diagrams then form the image of S∩T under the two displayed maps and propose A_j=A_i∩A′_{i′}.

[TXT028-indices] The diagram targets are I and I′, but the image formula writes I×J. A direct map-type check, recorded separately for each reader who performed it, flags this unexplained naming change. The set pair visibly reads (i,j′), the first bottom definition reads A_i′, and the second bound is I′_{≤j}. These differences from the surrounding expected pattern triggered enlarged readings; none was repaired. The second diagram has a headless psi line and an ordinary downward phi arrow with a retraced upper shaft.

No date, title sheet, page-count statement or explicit verification request appears. The capital and subscript overprints remain the least secure portions.

checks.who: GPT-6 Astra Pro / R1; effort inherited, not separately exposed
checks.outcome: Target check only: the diagram labels phi:S→I and phi′:T→I′, so the restricted pair map has displayed-target type S∩T→I×I′. The manuscript instead writes I×J before identifying K as subset of I×I′; no equality J=I′ is supplied here. This flags a notational mismatch, not a reason to change J in the transcription. No proof that the intersection family is a figure was performed.

With displayed arrows phi:S→I and phi′:T→I′, their restricted pair on S∩T naturally has codomain I×I′. The written I×J therefore uses a different name, unless J denotes I′. This prompted renewed ink inspection and I×J was retained; no theorem correction was made.

checks.outcome: Under inclusion order, the relation requiring both equivalences is their set intersection and greatest common lower bound. On a two-point set, take one relation universal and the other equality: class intersections give equality while their join is universal. This checks the conditional order issue only; the author’s possibly reversed convention is not settled.
